name: Joya de Cerén Archaeological Site
description: Joya de Cerén is a farming village in western El Salvador, about 36 km northwest of San Salvador, that was buried under volcanic ash around AD 600. The ash preserved its homes, storehouses and even a plot of manioc, the oldest known example of the crop at a site in the Americas. Often called the "Pompeii of the Americas," it shows how ordinary Maya villagers lived.
